subject: Surge bridge evacuation and audit-stitch plan for private fleet maintenance
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
To: Acme Health <ops@acmehealth.com>, David Luu <david.luu@acmehealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Surge bridge evacuation and audit-stitch plan for private fleet maintenance

Hi team —

We have a proposed maintenance window for the private deployment that runs in your VPC next month. Objective is to apply a critical kernel + runtime micropatch across the private fleet with zero-customer-impact and full auditability for compliance. High-level plan below; attached are the runbook, network map and preflight checklist.

Planned window: 2026-11-02 02:00–06:00 PT (4h) — target low-traffic window.
Goals:
- Apply micropatch to inference runtime and NV kernel drivers.
- Avoid cold starts for in-flight sessions where possible.
- Provide audit stitch (deterministic telemetry snapshot) for SOC evidence and rollback validation.

Key pieces (summary):
1) Surge bridge (cross-connect) — temporary traffic funnel to a small warm pool to protect production storefronts while we rotate nodes. The bridge keeps existing connections alive and ensures GRPC session resumption.
2) Version shelving (non-destructive pinning) — we will mark current model/runtime variants as Shelved vA for the duration; nodes will be upgraded to vB and we keep vA metadata for instant rebind if we need to unpin.
3) KV/Prefix eviction policy — perform prefix snapshot and ephemeral KV flush in stages; snapshots are retained for 30 days for rollback verification.
4) Audit stitch — timestamped telemetry artifact (trace + token-level diffs) captured pre/post each canary to prove parity for compliance review.

Preflight items (see attachments):
- Network path validation to ensure cross-connects + ACLs allow the bridge subnet.
- Canary in us-west-2 with throttled traffic.
- Smoke tests: realtime latency and token-consistency checks.

Requests from Acme ops: please confirm if the bridge subnet 10.18.240.0/24 is acceptable and whether your NVA allows outbound port 2443 for the control plane agent. Also confirm the maintenance window or propose alternative.

Attachments:
- maintenance-runbook-v1.pdf (runbook and rollback decision matrix)
- private-network-map.vsdx
- preflight-checklist.xlsx

Thanks — Ire

--
Irene Choi
Senior Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
irene@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>, Acme Health <ops@acmehealth.com>, David Luu <david.luu@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Surge bridge evacuation and audit-stitch plan for private fleet maintenance

Irene / Acme —

Thanks for the clear plan. A few technical clarifications and requests from infra side to make rollback deterministic: 

1) Canary sizing: prefer two canaries spaced 30 minutes apart (canary-1: 5% traffic, canary-2: 10% traffic). Each canary run should produce an audit-stitch bundle. If any token delta > 0.5% compared to baseline, stop.

2) Shelving mechanics: shelving must be non-destructive metadata-only ops. Implementation: tag active image (runtime+model) with label shelved:vA-20261102 and retain registries for 72 hours post-window. Do not GC during that period.

3) KV policy: sequence of ops — snapshot -> compress -> stage on backup mount -> partial eviction (LRU on prefixes older than 6h) -> verify TTL rehydration. Include a hook to rehydrate a single user session for manual verification.

4) Network/bridge failover: the surge bridge will be announced via BGP with a lower local-pref; if BGP fails, we fall back to region-based routing. Need confirmation from Acme that their NVA allows BGP ASN 64512 and support for community tags.

5) Rollback checklist (if canary fails):
- Immediate: stop rollout, flip routing to shelved:vA labels, unpin nodes (rolling rebind).
- Short-term: redeploy previous kernel if needed; rehydrate KV snapshot to validate state.
- Post-mortem: collect audit-stitch artifacts and store in compliance bucket (retention 365d).

I attached a short patch-lifecycle snippet (in runbook) and a sample CLI sequence for the rebind. Happy to walk through in a quick call.

-Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Senior Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Acme Health <ops@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 8 Oct 2026 07:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Surge bridge evacuation and audit-stitch plan for private fleet maintenance

Irene / team —

Operational confirmations:
- We can staff the runbook: Monica (lead on-call), Two SREs (2:00–10:00 PT), and an infra engineer for the BGP/bridge change window.
- Preflight timeline: 10/30 run a full dry-run against a staging slice; 11/01 final smoke run against canary slice.
- Rollout cadence: 15m per pod group, pause after every 3 groups for telemetry review.

Please add the following to the runbook before final signoff:
- Exact SLIs to monitor (p50/p95 latency, error-rate per-route, token-consistency mismatch rate).
- Emergency unpin shortcut and who is authorized to trigger it (Jonas and Monica).
- Contact matrix: add Acme's oncall and our oncall aliases; include escalation to support@redwood.ai.

Also note: we need to capture audit-stitch artifacts to a compliance bucket that uses customer-scoped encryption keys. Jonas — can you confirm the KMS policy allows writing artifacts with Acme's KID?

Monica

--
Monica Patel
Principal SRE, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.ai

Attachments: preflight-checklist.xlsx
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Health <ops@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Oct 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Surge bridge evacuation and audit-stitch plan for private fleet maintenance

All —

Approved from a governance and risk perspective. A few small asks before we lock: 
- Compliance artifact list: audit-stitch (trace package), signed runbook snapshot, and per-node package checksum list. Those three items must be snapshot-stamped and uploaded to the compliance bucket immediately after window.
- Retention: keep the audit artifacts for 13 months (SOC cadence).
- Please include an evidence checklist for SOC 2 reviewers (we'll attach the checklist to the runbook).

Jonas and I will be the emergency unpin authorizers. Monica — coordinate the on-call rota and ensure support@redwood.ai alias is reachable for the window.

If Acme wants to brief their security reviewer, I'll join the call — happy to do a 30-minute alignment.

Thanks — Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Director, Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.ai
